title: CLCON/404/2020 of NARENDRA KUMAR Vs NAMAMI BANSAL

paras.text:
CLCON No.404 of 2020
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Shakti Singh, Advocate for the petitioner.
A PIL was instituted before this Court being
Writ Petition (PIL) No.65 of 2011, Kunwar Pal Singh
State of Uttarakhand and others which was connected
with another Writ Petition (PIL) No.29 of 2016,
Preetam Singh vs. State of Uttarakhand and others.
These two PILs were connected together and were
decided by the Division Bench of this Court by the
judgment of 13.06.2018 whereby certain directions
were issued as contained in para 6 of the said judgment
of the Division Bench, which is quoted hereunder:-
6. Accordingly, the following mandatory
directions are issued to the State Government:-
A. The State Government is directed to remove
all the encroachments from the village
ponds/johars, play grounds and common grazing
land within a period of six months from today.
B. The State Government is also directed
through Secretary Revenue to ensure that all the
illegal entries changing the nature of the ponds/
common grazing land/ johar are reversed and the
land is restored to its original nature, and if
necessary, by carrying out digging up operations.
C. The State Government is also directed
through the respective SDMs to ensure that all
the johars/ponds/water bodies are fenced and
protected.
D. The State Government through office of
Chief Secretary is directed to ensure that
henceforth, no johar/ponds/water bodies/
common grazing land is encroached by anyone
through the State of Uttarakhand.
E. The State Government is also directed to
ensure that no sewerage flows into the water
bodies and their water quality is maintained

throughout the year. The endeavor of the State
Government should be to restore the village
ponds/water bodies, as they existed in the year
1951 when the U.P. Z.A. & L.R. Act was made
applicable.
G. The Sub Divisional Magistrates of the
respective areas are directed to constitute a
Committee comprising of six members including
the Pradhan of the Panchayat to identify and
locate the ponds/water bodies in their respective
jurisdiction."
The contention of the petitioner in the present
contempt petition is that for the purposes of seeking its
compliance for the removal of encroachment, which he
alleges to have been made on Khasra No.203 situated
in Village Rehmatpur, he had approached the Sub
Divisional Magistrate, by filling a representation on
03.10.2020; but the fact also which is revealed from
records is that he had also preferred writ petition being
Writ Petition No.1925 of 2020; in relation to the same
Khasra number wherein praying for a writ of
mandamus for removal of encroachment of the private
respondents from the aforesaid land. The said writ
petition was dismissed by this Court by the judgment
of 20.10.2020 holding thereof that since it entails a
factual determination of rights the remedy available to
the petitioner would be to approach before the Civil
Court or the Revenue Court. The said judgment was
rendered on 20.10.2020. The following directions was
issued:-
"The petitioner, in these present Writ Petitions, had
sought a writ of mandamus praying for removal of the
alleged encroachment of the private respondents in the
respective Writ Petitions, which they contend that they
have encroached upon Khasra No. 203, having an area of
0.1540 of Mauza Rahmatpur, Roorkee, District
Haridwar, and in the connected Writ Petition No. 1927
of 2020, it is alleged that the respondents have
encroached upon khasra No. 120, which according to the
petitioner it is a nala, recorded in revenue records.
Looking to the nature of relief sought in the pleadings

raised, since it is exclusively entailing a determination of
an evidence and appreciation of the respective case of the
private parties, the appropriate remedy which would be
available to the petitioner under law would be to
approach the competent Civil Court or even the Revenue
Court, as available to him under the provisions of the
U.P. Z.A. & L.R. Act, for redressal of his grievance. The
Writ remedy under Article 226 of the Constitution of
India for adjudicating of civil rights as against the
private individual cannot be invoked. Hence, the Writ
Petitions are dismissed with the liberty open to the
petitioner to approach the competent Civil Court or the
Revenue Court for redressal of his grievance, as available
to him under law."
During the course of hearing, this contempt
petition, the counsel for the petitioner very candidly
has submitted that the representation of 03.10.2020
was a subject matter of the writ petition, also which
was dismissed on 20.10.2020. He further submits that
since the judgment of the Division Bench dated
13.06.2018 is still surviving, this contempt petition at
his behest would be tenable.
The Registry has reported that the contempt
petition is barred by Section 20 of the Contempt of
Courts Act for the moment even if it is believed that as
a consequence of the judgment, which has been sought
to be enforced may be that it was having a recurring
cause of action or a continuous cause of action, the
contempt would lie, but in the present set of
circumstances, the contempt would not be maintainable
for the reason being that the petitioner himself almost
for the same set of facts and relief, had already
approached the writ court whereby his writ petition
was dismissed and thereafter to override the effect of
the judgment dated 20.10.2020, he cannot be permitted
to invoke the contempt jurisdiction under Section 12 of
the Contempt of Courts Act.
In that view of the matter, this Court is of the
view that filing of the contempt on 01.11.2020, after
the dismissal of the writ petitioner, he has nothing but a
clever device to over ride the effect of the judgment

20.10.2020 and in fact, it has been rather argued also
by the counsel for the petitioner that approaching the
Civil or the Revenue Court would be entailing very
prolonged proceedings, which in itself cannot be a
reason for not approaching the Civil Court or the
Revenue Courts as directed for an appropriate
determination of rights as was claimed in the writ
petition, preferred by the petitioner by way of writ of
mandamus.
For the reasons aforesaid, I decline to invoke my
powers under Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts
Act as no deliberate and intentional contempt is made
out. Consequently, the contempt petition is dismissed.
